title: The Guiana Shield: flat-topped mountains older than the Andes
goal: Describe the tepuis and what matters about them, using cleft sentences to put one idea in the spotlight.

sections.title: The Guiana Shield: flat-topped mountains older than the Andes
body: In this lesson you read about the Guiana Shield, an ancient rock region in the north of South America, and about the tepuis, the flat-topped mountains that rise over the jungle. You also read about the Angel Falls and about the mercury that illegal gold mining puts into the rivers.
The grammar is one you know: cleft sentences, which put one piece of information in the spotlight. The screens and instructions are in English; the readings are in Spanish.

items: I can put one idea in the spotlight with *lo que ... es* and *es/fue ... donde*, *quien*, *cuando*.
I can say what a tepuy is and what makes it special.
I can use the new words for plateaus, waterfalls and mercury.
